analysis.investment_thesis: Landmark Global is a tiny INR 52 Cr immigration consultancy earning a negligible 0.21% ROE — essentially no earning power on equity — despite an optically cheap 5.25x P/E. This is a fair business at a seemingly cheap price, precisely the value trap I teach investors to avoid.
key_strengths: Promoter holding 72.44% — meaningful skin in the game
Headline P/E of 5.25x avoids any IPO-hype premium
Asset-light consultancy model with low capital intensity
key_risks: ROE of 0.21% indicates the business creates almost no value on equity
Micro-cap INR 52 Cr — illiquid, no institutional coverage (FII 0%)
Immigration consultancy has no moat; subject to visa-policy and regulatory whim
red_flags: Near-zero ROE combined with low P/E suggests collapsed earnings and a mechanical multiple, not genuine cheapness
No FII and minimal DII (3.37%) — smart money has passed
analysis.detailed_analysis:
A 0.21% return on equity tells you everything you need to know — this business earns less on its capital than a savings account. The 5.25x P/E looks tempting, but with earnings this thin, a small operational hiccup flips it to a loss, and a low multiple on trivial profits is still trivial value. Immigration consulting is a service business with no switching costs, no brand moat, and heavy dependence on shifting visa regimes in Canada, the US, UK, and Australia — outside my circle of competence for durable economics.

At INR 52 Cr market cap with 72% promoter holding, this is effectively a closely-held micro-cap where minority shareholders have little say and liquidity is poor. I don't see a durable competitive advantage, I don't see capable capital allocation (evidenced by the ROE), and I don't see a margin of safety — a cheap multiple on near-zero earnings is not a margin of safety. I'd pass and wait for a wonderful business at a fair price instead.
